pairs.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/frame.test.tsx:53 The source guard on DealReview.tsx reads raw text with no comment stripping, so a comment containing `await closeThisWindow()` would keep this presence check green after the real call at DealReview.tsx:302 was deleted, while sibling guards such as reasons.test.ts do strip comments.

techniques.evidence: apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/frame.test.tsx:53 Presence assertion over unnormalised source (read at line 52). The technique requires the presence assertion to be normalised to code, and the file does not state that over-detection is the safe direction.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/review/Checks.tsx:20 A wait line is an announced, counted skip: it stays in the total and is not read as a pass. gating.ts:109 refuses when the checklist is empty (checks.length > 0). This is a runtime approval gate, applied by analogy to the pipeline wording.

apps/desktop/client/src/windows/approval/review/Checks.tsx:2 The component maps over the wallet's own enumeration with no hand-walked subset. Not-applicable lines fold into a counted line with a Show control, so none disappear silently.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path frames gates as pipeline and merge machinery, yet policy-projection and unmeasurable-criteria fit in-product refusal gates such as an approval checklist equally well; the subject should state whether product-runtime gates are in scope.
